prompts:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: a directly usable original hospital floor map background for a playable 2D JRPG.
Canvas: exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, landscape 3:2.
Projection: classic orthogonal three-quarter top-down 2D JRPG map. Look downward enough to see all walkable floor and the front faces of north walls and furniture. Every horizontal edge remains horizontal; every vertical room division remains vertical; scale is uniform over the entire map. No vanishing point, no first-person or interior-perspective illustration, no cinematic camera, no isometric diamond grid. All rooms are axis-aligned rectangles.
Style: fine 32-bit Japanese JRPG pixel tile art, sharp pixel clusters and economical cel shading, no blur or painterly rendering. Original architecture and props.
Exact floor plan: three rooms across the upper half, a broad continuous horizontal corridor across the middle, and three rooms across the lower half. The upper rooms are open along their lower edges onto the corridor. The lower rooms are open along their upper edges onto the corridor. Keep these six entrances wide and unobstructed, with clear continuous floor connecting them. Room divisions are at approximately one-third and two-thirds of the map width.
UPPER LEFT ROOM: a four-bed inpatient ward, exactly four empty hospital beds positioned near the side walls, with a generous aisle between them and a wide clear entry from the central corridor.
UPPER MIDDLE ROOM: a nurses' station, with a compact desk counter and medicine storage against the far wall, leaving most floor clear.
UPPER RIGHT ROOM: the director's office, with a desk, empty chair, bookcase and filing cabinet against walls, leaving a clear central floor.
CENTRAL CORRIDOR: broad level teal-grey tiled floor running uninterrupted from far left to far right, occupying roughly the middle fifth of the image. At its far left end, a water dispenser and wall telephone stand against the wall; at its far right end, a stairwell doorway and a short visible flight of stairs connect to the corridor. Do not place obstacles in the main walking route.
LOWER LEFT ROOM: an emergency treatment room, exactly two empty treatment beds with small medical equipment near the walls and a wide clear walking aisle.
LOWER MIDDLE ROOM: a records and research office, shelving full of plain case files and a work desk along the side and lower walls, with clear walking floor in the middle.
LOWER RIGHT ROOM: a duty break room, with a sofa, compact table and lockers kept near the side or lower walls, with clear floor at its entrance and center.
Materials and palette: blue-grey and teal-grey square floor tiles with subtle natural joints, muted pale hospital walls, practical furniture, warm amber lamps, deep blue night windows. Bright enough that every floor route, bed, doorway, and furniture footprint is immediately readable. Restrained dark-hospital atmosphere without blood or gore.
Constraints: empty map, no characters or people, no text or readable labels, no numbers, no letters, no UI, no dialogue boxes, no icons, no editor grid lines, no arrows, no logo or watermark. Do not obscure floor with dramatic shadows. Do not draw a cutaway poster, a room perspective painting, a title screen, a website, or a game screenshot with interface. This is one continuous walkable floor-map asset for code to add collision and characters. Generate exactly one image.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: functional correction to an existing playable 2D JRPG hospital floor map.
Input image: the provided original hospital floor map is the ONLY edit target. Preserve its exact 1536 x 1024 canvas, orthogonal top-down JRPG projection, scale, blue-grey tiles, warm lamps, night palette, all rooms, beds, furniture, walls, and image positions except the two obstructions described below.
Change ONLY the lower-middle records room's corridor entrance and the lower-right duty break room's corridor entrance. These are functional passage repairs.
LOWER-MIDDLE RECORDS ROOM: the horizontal central corridor is immediately above this room. Remove the row of bookcases directly behind its upper entrance, around x=550..920, y=600..710. Relocate those bookcases against the LEFT wall or available LOWER wall of the same records room, without moving the existing work desk. Make a broad, uninterrupted strip of the existing teal-grey floor tile extend from the central horizontal corridor straight through the upper entrance and down into the clear center of this room. The clear entrance and route must be at least 120 pixels wide in the original 1536-pixel canvas. No cabinet, sill, raised threshold, wall or other prop may block this route.
LOWER-RIGHT BREAK ROOM: remove the window-bearing wall segment directly behind its upper entrance, around x=1140..1310, y=590..680. Relocate the window to the RIGHT side wall of that room. Extend the same existing floor tiles continuously from the central corridor through the cleared upper opening into the room. The walkable opening must be at least 120 pixels wide, with no remaining sill or wall blocking it. Preserve the existing table, chairs, sofa, lockers and other furniture in their original places.
Invariants: keep every pixel outside these two localized room-entrance repair areas and the necessary furniture/window relocation areas unchanged as closely as possible. Keep the entire upper row of rooms, all six beds, the central corridor, left water dispenser and telephone, right stairwell, lower-left emergency room, and room boundaries unchanged. Do not redesign, relight, crop, restyle, shift, enlarge, or regenerate the overall map. Preserve the sharp pixel-art rendering. No people, text, labels, UI, arrows, grid overlay, logo or watermark. Output one repaired map as a new image.
assets.processing: Room crops placed at equal pixel scale; props use separate footprint and occlusion masks.

prompts:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production-ready four-direction walking sprite sheet for a playable 2D JRPG.
Canvas and transparency: exactly 1024 x 1024 pixels, PNG with a genuinely transparent alpha background. All space outside the sprites is completely transparent. Do not draw a checkerboard, white background, colored background, floor, ground, shadow, border, cell lines, letters, or numbers.
Grid: exactly FOUR columns by FOUR rows, sixteen sprites total. Each invisible cell is exactly 256 x 256 pixels. Every sprite is centered at x=128 inside its cell, with a consistent feet anchor near y=232 and head top near y=32. Maintain identical body scale, identity, clothing, and 2.5-head-tall proportions in all sixteen cells. Leave ample transparent gutter so hair, hands, shoes, and coat stay completely within each cell.
Character: one original adult Chinese female resident doctor with short dark brown hair, a small teal hair clip, white doctor's coat over a teal-green inner shirt, deep navy trousers, and brown shoes. Kind but focused anime face. No writing on clothing, no badge, no weapons.
Style: Original 32-bit Japanese JRPG pixel-sprite aesthetic, with readable square pixel clusters, crisp outlines, carefully limited cel-shaded colors, a cute large anime head and 2.5-head-tall chibi body. Clearly adult character designs despite chibi proportions. Practical modest clothing. Designed as usable game sprites, never poster illustrations or portraits.
Directions, strict row order:
ROW 1: FRONT VIEW, facing downward toward the viewer in every cell.
ROW 2: LEFT SIDE VIEW, facing screen-left in every cell.
ROW 3: BACK VIEW, facing upward away from the viewer in every cell.
ROW 4: RIGHT SIDE VIEW, facing screen-right in every cell.
Animation, strict column order within EVERY row:
COLUMN 1: clear left-foot-forward walking step, opposite arm swinging forward.
COLUMN 2: neutral standing pose with both feet together and arms resting.
COLUMN 3: clear right-foot-forward walking step, opposite arm swinging forward.
COLUMN 4: neutral standing pose with both feet together and arms resting, matching column 2.
Walking motion must be visible in both arms and legs, with consistent foot baseline and no sideways drift. The fourth sprite in each row is a standing pose, not a fourth direction. Whole bodies including shoes must remain fully visible.
Constraints: exactly sixteen separate sprites, no extra sprites, no alternate costume, no portraits, no cut-off body parts, no rendered labels, no decorative effects or props. Generate exactly one transparent sprite-sheet image.
assets.processing: Mechanical 4 by 4 packing; preserved generated alpha; fixed foot anchors.
